stops.name: Tai-chi school — Hangzhou
stops.detail:
Eight nights at a **sample tai-chi school** in the tea hills west of the lake: two sessions a day, simple rooms, meals in the school canteen. The school collects you from the station inn on the Sunday morning; Monday to Saturday is training, and **Sunday is the free day** for the lake, the temples and laundry.

The city is easy: the metro reaches the lake shore, and the tea villages are a bus ride up the valley. Evenings are early — lights out around 21:30.

stops.name: Shanghai
stops.whenLabel: Mon Mar 29 → Fri Apr 2 · two beds
stops.detail:
Four nights in the big city, in two beds: two nights by the Bund, two in a lane house near Xintiandi. The **Shanghai Museum East** is the one thing that needs a ticket ahead — it is **closed on Mondays**, so the visit is Tuesday. Wednesday is a guided walk out to the water town of Zhujiajiao.

Everything else is the metro and your feet: the Bund at night, Yu Garden in the morning before the crowds, the plane-tree streets of the old French Concession in the afternoon.

stops.detail:
Two nights in the garden city between Shanghai and the mountains. The shape is simple: the Friday train out of Shanghai, Saturday for the **Humble Administrator's Garden** and the canal lanes, and Sunday back to Shanghai Hongqiao for the evening flight to Huangshan.

The bed is booked: a **sample hostel on Pingjiang Road**, a canal-side lane with teahouses. The garden ticket is timed and sells out on spring weekends, so it carries a dated task.

stops.name: Huangshan
stops.whenLabel: Sun Apr 4 → Wed Apr 7 · 2n mountain + 1n town
stops.address: 安徽省黄山市黄山区汤口镇
stops.detail:
Granite peaks, crooked pines and a sea of cloud — the mountain every Chinese landscape painting is quietly about. Two nights at the foot of the mountain in Tangkou, one in the old town of Tunxi.

The park pass covers two days *(verify when buying)*. The cableways save the knees; the stone steps are the real way up and down. Spring mornings are the clear ones — start early.

stops.name: Hong Kong & Macau
stops.detail:
Four nights to finish: the harbour, the hills and a day in Macau. Hong Kong is outside the mainland visa count, takes **Hong Kong dollars**, writes in **Traditional characters** and speaks Cantonese. Google Maps works here; the MTR goes everywhere.

Macau is an hour by ferry: the old Portuguese centre in the morning, Coloane village and its egg tarts in the afternoon.

infoCards.heading: Visa — the one number that matters
items: Sample rule: **25 days visa-free** on the mainland (a demo figure, not a real policy).
The count starts **the day AFTER entry**. Entry Mar 20 → day 1 is Mar 21.
**Deadline: Apr 14, 24:00.** Planned exit Apr 13 = day 24, a one-day buffer.
Hong Kong and Macau are separate and do not count.

infoCards.heading: The 20 kg rule
items: Every domestic flight allows **20 kg** checked — pack to 20, not 23.

infoCards.heading: Power banks
items: Carry-on only, with a visible capacity label (3C mark on the mainland).

infoCards.heading: Airport traps
items: Apr 4 flies from **Hongqiao (SHA)**, not Pudong.
Shanghai has two airports far apart — check the code, every time.

infoCards.heading: Trains
items: The passport IS the ticket. Use the manual lane 人工通道, arrive 45 min early.

infoCards.heading: Money
items: Phone payments everywhere on the mainland; carry ¥500 cash for the hike.
Hong Kong: Octopus card; Macau takes HKD at par.

infoCards.heading: Internet
items: A roaming eSIM avoids most blocks; download maps before leaving wifi.
